SPEC CONFLICT (decision needed from the orchestrator): the Webhooks pre-check says the body must have a MAPPED event_type (failure -> invalid row, 400) while the event list says 'Unknown types -> ignored'. I followed the task's acceptance criterion: an unmapped type is a pre-check failure (invalid row EVENT_TYPE_NOT_MAPPED, 400), because it is the only reading that keeps SEC-6's 'no provider call for junk'. Consequence: a PayPal webhook subscribed to extra event types gets 400 and PayPal retries those until it gives up; the README/runbook must say to subscribe the webhook to the seven mapped events only. If the orchestrator prefers 'ignored', it is a one-line change in precheck() (keep a well-formed string, drop the mapped check, let applyEvent return ignored) and the test table in 'SEC-6: ... event_type that is not mapped'.

A body with a leading BOM is accepted by the route (parsed without it, verified as the exact bytes). The fake adapter verifies it (HMAC over the bytes); the Sandbox adapter answers ok {verified:false} for it (JSON.parse refuses a BOM), so on the Sandbox such a body is an invalid row and 400 without a provider call (tested). PayPal does not send a BOM, so this affects only a hand-made request. Whitespace outside the object is passed through unchanged; the Sandbox double verifies the member span, so a whitespace-wrapped body signed over all bytes would not verify there (e1's note (h)); not tested at the stub.

Rate counter rows: an admitted request inserts one rate_events row (kind webhook, key ip:<key>); the route deletes that key's expired rows on each request, and retention.js purges rate_events older than 24 h. A flood from many distinct IPv6 /64 prefixes leaves one row each until retention runs (bounded by 60 per key per minute).

NOTES FOR e4/e6. e4 (reconciler, saga): a webhook can move an operation without the reconciler: authorization_pending|approved|unknown(prev ok) -> authorized (+ provider_authorization_id, authorization_expires_at, the resolution hook), authorized -> voided, authorized|capture_pending -> captured (+ provider_capture_id), authorized -> capture_pending, capture_pending -> authorized (denied), refund_pending -> refunded (+ provider_refund_id). It clears unknown_since when it moves an unknown operation, leaves prev_status as it was and does NOT touch provider_calls rows: an open unknown/intent call row of that operation stays for the reconciler, which must therefore treat 'the operation is already past that state' as a resolved call (CAS on status, no error), exactly like recordCall's authorize/void mappers already do. A capture event moves an operation outside the saga lease; the saga must re-read the operation status after its capture call and accept captured as done. Webhook rows never reach the reconciler; it keeps polling (webhooks are secondary). The admin timeline already reads webhook_events (source 'webhook', detail outcome/signatureStatus/flagged). Flagged rows (outcome flagged, flagged = 1, flag_reason) are the operator's list; nothing else reads them yet. e6: the route answers 200 {outcome: applied|ignored|flagged|duplicate, requestId}; errors 400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID (no details), 404 NOT_FOUND, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, 429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit webhook_ip + Retry-After, 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE + Retry-After 30 (and 503 DB_BUSY). Tests sign with signEvent({event|rawBody, transmissionTime: <harness clock ISO>}) and the harness env must set RS_FAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to FAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (the fake otherwise generates a random key in meta). The harness clock is fixed at 2026-10-20T06:00:00Z, so the signer's default new Date() transmission time is outside the 15-minute window: always pass transmissionTime.
